title: 28th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: This 3 December 2025 sitting (9:01 to 10:35) was the last before the Majlis's winter recess. Members voted on three presidential ambassador nominations (Jordan, Palestine and Japan), amendments to the Tourism Act, the new Zakat Bill, a rules amendment, an amendment to the Drugs Act and the removal of a Criminal Court judge, and all of them passed. The attendance figures in item 2 (30 present, 2 on leave, 4 on official travel) look low against the 60 to 66 members who voted later, so treat them with caution. The Speaker closed the sitting with a summary of the session's work.

items.title: Closing remarks by the Speaker on the session's work and start of the recess

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the Japan nominee as experienced, citing the committee's review and the long-standing ties between Japan and the Maldives.
Supported the Tourism Act amendments, calling tourism the economy's mainstay, and said the Majlis keeps working at pace up to the recess.
Said the Zakat Bill is a brand-new law, thanked the committee and its earlier rapporteur, and backed the council and fund it creates.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Presented the General Committee report on the Majlis rules amendment (Rule 23 and Rule 30).
Presented the Judiciary Committee report finding the Judicial Service Commission followed due process in the request to remove a Criminal Court judge.
Presented the Judiciary Committee report on the Drugs Act amendment bill, which the committee passed unanimously.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report on the Jordan and Palestine non-resident ambassadors, saying the committee had studied both candidates and found them suitable.
Presented the committee report on the Japan ambassador nominee, noting the interview and checks against Foreign Service Act requirements.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Backed the Japan nominee but argued ambassadors should be honest, non-partisan appointees and that diplomatic posts should not serve as political rewards.
On the Tourism Act, supported the changes and said skilled Maldivian youth are scarce in the industry and need training so fewer foreign workers are hired.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Presented the Economic Committee report on the Tourism Act amendments: views were sought from five bodies and the committee held several meetings before approving the bill.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said the amendments let state-linked companies get resort leases and require training resorts; urged transparent dealings and warned the Maldivian share of tourism jobs is falling, now below about 40 percent.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Supported the Tourism Act changes, saying state-linked companies running resorts could return profits and better jobs to Maldivians, and urged ministries to bring in the follow-up rules quickly.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Presented the Social Committee report on the Zakat Bill: the committee gathered views, held several meetings, made amendments and approved the bill unanimously.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the Zakat Bill, noting zakat is an Islamic pillar and that a law should raise awareness, especially about zakat on wealth.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported the report, saying a law is the right route for zakat; stressed awareness, getting funds to rightful recipients with dignity, and staffing the new bodies with capable people.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Supported the Drugs Act bill, saying it lets new drug types be listed and adds tougher penalties, including a death sentence for large imports that needs a unanimous Supreme Court bench.

decisions: The minutes of the 22nd to 24th sittings were approved without amendment.
The President's letter on joining the Labour Centre of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation was referred to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The Majlis approved Dr Hala Hameed as non-resident ambassador to Jordan and Dr Ibrahim Zuhuree as non-resident ambassador to Palestine.
The Majlis approved Ahmed Mukhloof as the Maldives' ambassador to Japan.
The Tourism Act (99/2) amendment bill passed its third reading.
The Zakat Bill passed its third reading.
The amendment to the Majlis rules of procedure (Rule 23 and Rule 30) was passed.
The Majlis voted to remove Criminal Court judge Hussain Faiz Rashad from office.
The Drugs Act (2011/17) amendment bill passed its third reading.
In closing, the Speaker said the Majlis held 28 sittings of about 64 hours this session, plus 142 committee meetings, and passed 15 bills; the recess starts from this sitting.
